video_title: Micah Nori Media Availability | Oct. 19, 2026 | Portland Trail Blazers

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon's concussion symptoms and recovery timeline
quotes.excerpt: he still has those symptoms with the headaches. He's had one before and he said it's following that course.
quotes.quote: He's good. We saw him today this morning. He still has those symptoms with the headaches. He's had one before and he said it's following that course. So hopefully he will be okay, but still not 100% right. He's got one heck of a big fat lip and obviously with the concussion symptoms and that, but he'll be okay.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori provides an update on Brandon, noting he is still dealing with concussion symptoms and headaches. He says the player is following a recovery course but is not yet 100 percent.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Injury updates on Chris Youngblood and Mica
quotes.excerpt: Chris Youngblood with his Achilles. He should be, he practiced a little bit today.
quotes.quote: The only other one I think is Chris Youngblood with his Achilles. He should be, he practiced a little bit today. And Mica is still getting himself back from just being sick on the road there at the end, and just getting him back up to fully healthy.
quotes.social_post: Injury update from Micah Nori: Chris Youngblood is back to practicing with his Achilles issue, while Mica is working his way back to full health after being sick.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: The team's focus on collective rebounding effort
quotes.excerpt: I like how Rob put it yesterday. He said we need to f-ing rebound.
quotes.quote: I like how Rob put it yesterday. He said we need to f-ing rebound. Is that just an effort thing? And if it's not, how do you go about addressing it? No, I think that rebounding is always effort, but then there does come into a, I mean, I could be trying as hard as I can to rebound, but you're bigger, stronger than me, you're just going to keep on holding me off. So some of these things, it's more so helping each other rebound.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the team rebounding struggles: Rebounding is always about effort, but it is also about helping each other out because sometimes you are just going to get held off by a bigger, stronger player.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Implementing rebounding drills and finishing possessions
quotes.excerpt: every drill is a passing drill. There's no difference now, every drill ends with a rebound.
quotes.quote: They say back in the day every drill is a passing drill. So you want to make sure that every pass is on time, on target. There's no difference now, every drill ends with a rebound. So talk about finishing possessions and we're imploring guys to crash so that we get a good feel and a good look at what it looks like and what it feels like. And so every single drill that we do live, whether it be half court or up and down, just finishing it off and making sure we play it all the way through the possession.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the team is emphasizing finishing possessions in practice, noting that every drill now ends with a rebound to ensure players are crashing the glass.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: The benefits of playing live scrimmages for team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: they played together so they see what it looks like full speed all the combinations.
quotes.quote: I think the one thing that we've done a good job of is playing and making sure that these guys get used to playing. So it's twofold. One, they played together so they see what it looks like full speed all the combinations. But also to get into basketball shape. It's a lot different than back in the day everybody just runs 17s and all this type of thing and suicides that they used to call back in the day. But now it's just more playing and we've done a really good job, I feel, the staff has and the H&P staff of keeping us up to date on, hey, we can go another one, these three guys need to play one more five-minute little scrimmage.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori explains the team's shift toward live scrimmaging over traditional conditioning drills to build chemistry and get players into basketball shape.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: City's defensive versatility and physical conditioning
quotes.excerpt: Dale and Greg are our main strength conditioning guys and they've done a really good job.
quotes.quote: Dale and Greg are our main strength conditioning guys and they've done a really good job of just looking into the biomechanics, the movements, this and that. Looking at what body type they are number one, how they can get them as physically fit and they do and especially a guy when you look at a guy like City, he's one that we're asking to defend damn near five positions. So it's not like he can just be big bulk up for fives and all this type. He's got to guard some smalls and so I just think that they've really done a good job.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori discusses the physical demands on City, who is being asked to defend nearly five positions, requiring a balance between strength and mobility.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Expanding City's offensive role and shooting development
quotes.excerpt: he works very hard with John Townson and the PD guys and the one thing about City's shot.
quotes.quote: He works very hard with John Townson and the PD guys and the one thing about City's shot is when he misses, he misses long and short. And we've talked about that before. You got to worry about guys that miss left and right. So he has a chance to be a pretty good catch and shoot guy and he's worked on that. But what's going to keep him on the floor is exactly what you said first Sean, his energy, his effort, his defensive capabilities.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says City has potential as a catch and shoot player, but his value to the team remains his energy, effort, and defensive capabilities.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: The team's genuine camaraderie and lack of cliques
quotes.excerpt: the fact the camaraderie and just that, I mean, there's no fakeness about it.
quotes.quote: I think the fact the camaraderie and just that, I mean, there's no fakeness about it. And what I mean by that is you don't have to like all your teammates. You do have to respect them and you have to get along. But there's, I mean, but these guys are really easy to like. And what's cool is there's no cliques. I mean, they all, obviously sometimes they gravitate towards their age and when they've come in this and that, but I mean, the groups that you see talking in the train room that you see talking on the side of the court, I mean, it could be any mix and match of anyone.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praises the team chemistry, noting there are no cliques and that the players are genuinely easy to like and respect.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: The strategic value of using ATOs for player engagement
quotes.excerpt: I think it helps players stay engaged number one in the timeouts and helps them to lock in.
quotes.quote: I think it helps players stay engaged number one in the timeouts and helps them to lock in to carry out what you're doing on the floor. And you also want to try to help somebody get an easy one. And then there's also times you run ATOs, you know, for a to money to make sure that, you know, if he's doing all the dirty stuff, dirty work as far as just rebounding, guarding the best player, he deserves some shots too.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on ATO strategy: It is about keeping players engaged and rewarding those who do the dirty work, like rebounding and defending, with scoring opportunities.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Emphasizing sacrifice and collective responsibility within the team
quotes.excerpt: brutal truths is the one thing I learned from Chris Finch and what I mean by that.
quotes.quote: Brutal truths is the one thing I learned from Chris Finch and what I mean by that is you're better off just, if it's fair and it's truthful and you follow through with it, then it's really hard for them to, they might be disappointed, but not to be pouty, upset and all that type of thing. But it's a good question because there has been no games yet, but that's what the relationship piece comes into it.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori shares his coaching philosophy learned from Chris Finch: If you are fair and truthful with players, it is hard for them to be pouty or upset.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: The team's plan to utilize a 10-man rotation
quotes.excerpt: I think that, um, I think for sure we will go, uh, 10 deep. Absolutely.
quotes.quote: I think that, um, I think for sure we will go, uh, 10 deep. Absolutely. And then, um, I just think, no, they don't. Um, and I just think that, uh, I think the way that our roster is set up, like some teams might be a little more top heavy talent wise and I'm saying maybe just front end loaded. I'm not saying their top eight is better than our top eight, but they might not have a nine and 10 that they feel comfortable playing. But I just really think and believe and I know our front office or coaching staff and even talking to the players, like, so if we go 10 deep, that gives each of you, you might lose two, three minutes, but that's those extra, you should be able to go to your point, be physically fit and play hard to whole time.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori confirms the team plans to go 10 deep in their rotation this season, citing the roster depth and the ability to maintain high intensity.
